output.name: Tessal
output.myth: When a boat did not come home, the women of the cliff set Tessal on the hearth, filled it with sea-water, and waited. Nobody sat by it. You do not sit beside a kettle for a drowned man; you put it on and get on with your mending. When Aun cut the string, the wind carried Tessal down the Leeward side, where the Gull Who Lost a Word watches it from a hand-span east and says nothing. Its spout points up at the Tallow Lamp, the light boats steer by. Tiru burns low to the south, where a mother flew her red kite for the boats still out. Kael casts past it every night and hauls up only steam, and grumbles. Hesk counts it each turn of the Reel and has never once seen it boil. That is the way of it. If it boils, the one out there is climbing the cliff path with wet boots and an empty belly, and someone had better have the tea ready. So keep the kettle full, child, and keep your hands busy.
output.finding: Find the Gull Who Lost a Word, then look a hand-span (about 20°) west of it to find Tessal, the Iron Kettle, low in the Leeward Reach.
